A second application exec was not present, so application concurrency is not required to produce this record. Launchd pid 1, launchctl pid 2, and the desktop pid 13 were already alive. code_signing_page_kill_excluded.detail: The spawn-time flags are 0x20020001, so CS_KILL and CS_HARD were clear at the csops status query. In pinned kern_cs.c, cs_invalid_page calls threadsignal with set_exitreason FALSE only after CS_KILL is set, including when cs_force_kill forces that bit, and that call does not build a reason. vm_fault.c then installs OS_REASON_CODESIGNING / CODESIGNING_EXIT_REASON_INVALID_PAGE when cs_killed is set. threadsignal with set_exitreason TRUE records the name exc handler. The captured reason is OS_REASON_SIGNAL code 9, built with a null procname argument while current_proc was pid 14, whose p_name is chonk-terminal-darwin. That is a different record from the page-kill path. The console's two cs_invalid_page lines are allow-and-clear-VALID for pid 1 and pid 2.

xnu_reasonless_sigkill.role: Separate from the qualification verdict. This is a source reading of sources/puredarwin-m1-desktop/src/Kernel/xnu. It is not proof that those bytes are kernel 02fe2d41.
xnu_reasonless_sigkill.how_the_record_is_built: psignal calls psignal_internal with a null reason. For SIGKILL, if the target thread's uu_exit_reason is null, kern_sig.c around 2447 builds build_signal_reason(signum, NULL) on the sending thread and installs it on the target thread. build_signal_reason records current_proc()'s pid and, when the procname argument is null, copies the whole p_name. The 6f70 tail matches that full-width copy.
can_run_as_the_victim_before_main_writes: kill() in kern_sig.c around 1411. A kill, kill of pid 0, or killpg issued by pid 14 enters psignal on pid 14's own thread and can do so from dyld or a libSystem initializer, before main creates a file. No such call was shown in app002; libSystem and dyld were not audited at binary level.

Any other psignal(SIGKILL) with a null reason invoked on a thread whose current_proc() is pid 14, with the reason then installed on pid 14. The sites below are the ones in this tree that can do that without an explicit reason namespace.

sites_checked.site: kern_proc.c CS_OPS_MARKINVALID around 3868 and CS_OPS_MARKKILL around 3896
sites_checked.fits_this_record: Only if the caller is pid 14 and the branch calls psignal. MARKINVALID calls psignal only when CS_KILL is already set. The spawn query shows CS_KILL clear. MARKKILL calls psignal only when CS_VALID is already clear. The spawn query shows CS_VALID set. A later flag change could arm either branch. No userspace caller was established at binary level.
These run on the thread that is inside the dirty-tracking update. They match when that thread is pid 14 and the shutdown-on-clean state is already set. They are not an automatic step of exec.
psignal runs as the suspend caller. It matches this sender only when that caller is pid 14.

sites_checked.site: process_policy.c proc_apply_resource_actions PROC_POLICY_RSRCACT_TERMINATE around 727, reached from task_policy.c task_action_cpuusage around 3074
sites_checked.fits_this_record: task_action_cpuusage is a thread_call. That call's current_proc() is the kernel thread-call context, so the recorded sender would be that context rather than pid 14.

sites_checked.site: task.c task_fatal_port_no_senders around 8635 and bsd_kern.c task_identity_token_try_sigkill around 120
sites_checked.fits_this_record: The only call of task_identity_token_try_sigkill is the no-senders handler, and that handler is compiled under CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS. It calls psignal on the proc named by the token, from whichever thread drops the last send right. It matches pid 14 only when that thread's current_proc() is pid 14. The fatal port is allocated from the mach-port hard-limit notification. If that allocation fails, task_self_sigkill uses psignal_with_reason and OS_REASON_RESOURCES, which is a different namespace. This read did not find CONFIG_PROC_RESOURCE_LIMITS set to 1 in the pinned headers, so inclusion in the booted kernel is not established. It is not an automatic path in the first 130 ms for a process that has not exhausted the port table.

kill takes the dext's owning proc and psignal's it with a null reason. The recorded sender is current_proc() of the caller. The in-tree caller besides a test is IOService.cpp around 4739, the DriverKit power-ack failure path. That matches pid 14 only if the caller thread is pid 14. The attempt 003 console has no IOUserServer or dext line. A freshly exec'd terminal does not enter this function on its own thread.

psignal(current_proc(), SIGKILL) runs only when kVNG_POLICY_SIGKILL is set and the exception-policy branch was not taken. The default policy takes the exception branch. The console shows policy initialization only, and the bootargs command line does not name vnguard.

sites_checked.site: kern_exit.c around 2620 and kern_proc.c pid_resume around 6712
sites_checked.fits_this_record: The exit path psignal's traced children from the tracer's thread, so the sender is the tracer. The resume path records the caller of pid_resume. Either matches this capture only when that caller is pid 14 and the reason is installed on pid 14. Neither is an automatic exec step.

does_not_produce_this_record: cs_invalid_page plus the vm_fault cs_killed path installs OS_REASON_CODESIGNING, and threadsignal(..., TRUE) names the sender exc handler.
psignal_with_reason paths that pass an explicit EXEC, CODESIGNING, JETSAM, GUARD, or RESOURCES reason.
xnu_reasonless_sigkill.open: The cause remains the set of null-reason psignal(SIGKILL) calls that can run with current_proc()==pid 14. The kill syscall on pid 14's own thread is the path that needs no extra kernel state. The other sites above need a flag change, a prior policy or port-limit event, or a caller that is already pid 14.
